Package model.description

Class DCursor

java.lang.Object
java.awt.geom.RectangularShape
java.awt.geom.Rectangle2D
java.awt.geom.Rectangle2D.Double
model.description.DCursor
All Implemented Interfaces:
Shape, Serializable, Cloneable
Direct Known Subclasses:
DRectangle
public class DCursor extends Rectangle2D.Double
The part of the description of a described formal that concerns local layout such as baseline length and writepoint (beginning of baseline). It separates the graphics and drawing part from the layout part together with the class that takes care of former. This is a semantic gift from separation of concerns and code readability, things that object oriented inheritance enforce.

It also is the only encapsulator or the formals value. This is a implementation choice to keep things at one place. In the future these values could well figure in other contexts such as doing arithmetic with them.

Although this object is for layout, rendering aspects currently present are underlying all their guages. Remember that many of it's set values could be pre-calculated averages and could be real depending on if the cursor is filled with a glyph or not. See FontMetrics.

  • Constructor Details

    • DCursor

      public DCursor(Rectangle2D.Double frame)
      This is the simplest constructor of object of this class and uses only a rectangle to compute layouting. Remember that base line reference point and other things rely on current graphics configuration, primarily chosen font. It makes a guess of its future use by using an average glyph when computing this. So the write point will probably change when it is filled.
      Parameters:
      frame - The frame that should fit an future glyph
      See Also:
      • CharGauge
      • PaintStatics.AVERAGE_ADVANCE

    • DCursor

      public DCursor(Placeholder frame)
      Creates an empty cursor from a placeholder frame. Since the place holder object and class is very rich, not just a rectangle it is merely a transfer of variables. The place holder could have a described formal in it's description part is not stored, only the value.
      Parameters:
      frame - The frame working as a preimage for this cursors size and layout.

    • DCursor

      public DCursor(Formal primitive, double baseline)
      Constructs a cursor that that fits a formal with a certain base line length. This cursor depends on this applications current configuration regarding fonts and windows such as size and type. So the descriptive aspect is still very much present implicitly.
      Parameters:
      primitive - The formal that this cursor should hold. Note that
      baseline - The length of the rendered glyph's baseline.

      public Point2D.Double getWritepoint()

    • getLocalReferencepoint

      public Point2D.Double getLocalReferencepoint()
      This gives the cursor's local reference point relative to it's upper left corner, in common device coordinate manner. 'Reference point' is typographica nomenclature while I guess 'writepoint' is just common programming jargon.
      Returns:
      The reference point of this cursor which could be a averaging guess of what it should contain and could also be properly set to a specific glyph. These things are settled by the constructor only at the time of writing.
      See Also:
      • FontMetrics

    • getAscendingBounds

      public Rectangle2D.Double getAscendingBounds()
      The bounds of the area from the base line and uppwards. So that descending parts falls outside of that area. It feel more intuitive to have a cursor that starts att the base although the glyph descends below it.
      Returns:
      The bounds of the area from the cursor's base line an uppwards (negative y-direction).

    • resizeToBaseline

      public void resizeToBaseline(double newbaseline)
      Resizes this cursor to a fit a new baseline. It uses it's current parameters as outset and does not revert to an averaging guess of a future glyph.
      Parameters:
      newbaseline - The new base line length.
